📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
  • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
  • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

It has been revealed that AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand noted everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Recent findings suggest that martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Sources indicate that significant chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

In a recent development, milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

Recent findings suggest that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by latest signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

According to recent reports, manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

According to recent reports, milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

In a recent development, manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

It has been revealed that fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Recent findings suggest that santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs.

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

In a recent development, A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Sources indicate that carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

It has been revealed that A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Industry observers note that estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Sources indicate that amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

In a recent development, milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

Sources indicate that united make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

According to recent reports, szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely latest cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

According to recent reports, marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

Aug 5: AC Milan 1 Inter Milan 1.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE.

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

Sources indicate that “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

Recent findings suggest that “Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

Jul 18: Manchester United 0 Wrexham 1.

Jul 24: Rosenborg 0 Manchester United 5.

Aug 1: Manchester United 2 Atlético Madrid 1.

Aug 8: Paris St-Germain 1 Manchester United 1.

Aug 12: Manchester United 1 Leeds United 1 (5-4 pens).

In a recent development, welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the massive ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri noted Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

In a recent development, kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (6021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
  • According to recent reports, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
  • In a recent development, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the upcoming signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

According to recent reports, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

In a recent development, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

According to recent reports, title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

Industry observers note that first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

In a recent development, another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

Sources indicate that “They are really good examples,” Arteta remarked. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

Industry observers note that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

According to recent reports, you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

Industry observers note that it can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

Sources indicate that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

According to recent reports, city, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where fresh boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Recent findings suggest that throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

In a recent development, had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal indicated was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

Industry observers note that arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

Referee Sam Barrott (Yorkshire).

Industry observers note that it’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

Sources indicate that I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

Sources indicate that A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

Industry observers note that I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

It has been revealed that the feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka.

The players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7.

In a recent development, what happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

In a recent development, we highlighted our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

In a recent development, we want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

Industry observers note that the league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

Industry observers note that marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

Sources indicate that just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

In a recent development, rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

Industry observers note that city have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

In a recent development, odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

It has been revealed that city’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

Nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

It has been revealed that chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

According to recent reports, better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

Chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

Sources indicate that cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

Odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

Arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

It has been revealed that city chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

Recent findings suggest that lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

In a recent development, city with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

In a recent development, arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a newly introduced look.

Sources indicate that arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

Sources indicate that christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was key to pull City’s defence out of shape.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

Man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

Industry observers note that so far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

In a recent development, looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two big hitters in midfield sharing the game.

Recent findings suggest that 7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ.

It has been revealed that 00:23 - Riccardo Calafiori's goal for Arsenal after 23 seconds is the first scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.Rapid. pic.twitter.com/FCwVKuTOlh.

Industry observers note that advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

“You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

According to recent reports, mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

Arsenal playing through the pitch and City’s defensive shape again, this time it was started by a fizzed Raya pass into Tzolis. Three on three, but Madueke’s shot is straight at Donnarummma. The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s defence stretched for the first time in the game. Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

Madueke with a tame shot on goal after O’Reilly went Awol defensively, but the flag was up for offside.

Arsenal come forward again, with Havertz holding the ball up well. Tzolis reverses a pass for Calafiori, but he anticipates a challenge in the area and is rightly booked for diving.

Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

It has been revealed that then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

It has been revealed that foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

It has been revealed that eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

According to recent reports, the Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

An ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

Recent findings suggest that the latest signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

Gvardiol slides across to win an notable challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

It has been revealed that arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

In a recent development, city soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

In these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU.

City’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

According to recent reports, the Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

Better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

Interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

It has been revealed that considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s big names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the fresh season approaches.

Arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

In a recent development, arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland.

Recent findings suggest that declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

It has been revealed that arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

Industry observers note that in truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer prepares remain up in the air for both camps.

City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

In a recent development, in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team. Sources indicate that camarda has had a tougher time after a loan spell at Lecce, but Milan have made it very clear through renewals and words that they will focus more on the youngsters. It’s exciting times as well, given how they have all performed with the U21 national team too.

Industry observers note that speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Italy’s U21 coach Silvio Baldini was asked about the breakthrough of Cisse, Camarda’s current state of mind and why Bartesaghi is a ‘luxury’ for his team. Safe to say that he likes the trio a lot.

In a recent development, cisse has had a proper breakthrough. Did you see that coming?

“Compared to a year ago, I can see a different guy, who’s more mature and prepared, with higher self-esteem, psychologically changed, simply stronger.

According to recent reports, “He has Milan to thank for signing him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and making room for him, then giving him consistent playing time. If he then makes the national team and does well, so much the better.”.

Milan deserve credit, and you also deserve credit for discovering him as a centre-forward….

In a recent development, “Analysing training sessions, a series of situations emerged where he managed to score by attacking space and depth: if you can do it on the right and left, it means you can also do it in the centre. But even there, the credit goes entirely to the staff.

“They had the intuition, realising that Cisse could be useful to our game system in that way and at the same time, allowing Alpha to discover a new role successfully. I’m simply honest and meritocratic in my choices.

“Even though the goal against Armenia actually came from him as a second striker, at the end of that match we had two centre-forwards, him and Camarda.”.

In a recent development, camarda, by the way, has struggled at Milan but scored for the U21s. How is that possible?

“I can only speak about the work we do together. I spoke to him at length, I dedicated time to him, I asked him to explain his concerns, his fear of not being able to express himself as he would like. I told him stories of my own life, of how I came out of it.

According to recent reports, “A dialogue not as a coach-player but as a son, or rather a grandson, as he could be, and a grandfather: from the heart. I’m not interested in performances as an end in themselves; they will come if he feels in the right place.

“I try to make him understand that I see him, I follow him in many small ways: he’s a conscientious boy who shouldn’t become obsessed with the goal, but rather experience football for what it is: fun.

“If, instead of fun, it becomes a test, then it worries you, and if you worry, you no longer enjoy it and it doesn’t help you perform at your best.”.

To have more fun, do you recommend that he should leave Milan for another team?

According to recent reports, “I’m not going to get involved in this. There are clubs, agents, and a family: they know what the best path will be for him. Let’s remember that he’s 18 years old, he plays for AC Milan and in the Under-21s.

“It’s clear that the more he plays, the better it will be for AC Milan and for everyone. We’re talking about a great player, a champion in my opinion, who needs to finish his development: he’s still growing, he already has a great eye for goal, and he’s sacrificing himself for the team.”.

Camarda-Cisse: Can Milan provide the national team with one of the forward duos of the future?

“For me, yes. I see them as a permanent fixture in the national team, and of course they need to prove it and earn it on the pitch. But they have all the characteristics to do it. I found Alpha to be better prepared, even in his game decisions. Amorim did well to develop him.”.

The third Rossoneri player is Bartesaghi: more of a full-back like with you or a winger like at Milan?

Sources indicate that “Davide is one of the best players in his position I’ve coached in many years. He’s talented, very professional, mature, introverted yet open, and that’s not a contradiction: he has enormous potential, and he reveals it every time he comes to us.

Industry observers note that “If I were any Serie A coach, I’d take him with me. For the Under-21s, Bartesaghi is a luxury. He plays with heart, passion, and intelligence, as well as possessing high-level technical, physical, and running skills.

Andoni Iraola's men have taken nine points from 12 on offer in Europe so far, good enough for eighth place in the Champions League rankings after their 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce last time out.

The Reds also return to European action on the back of a 4-0 demolition of Manchester United, rising into the top four of the Premier League table in the process.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their showdown with Club Brugge, who are just one place below Liverpool in the 36-team table courtesy of an inferior goals scored total.

In a recent development, possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton).

Cody Gakpo was a surprise absentee from the Liverpool squad against Man United, and Iraola subsequently revealed that the attacker had picked up a calf injury on Netherlands duty.

Gakpo is also expected to miss out in midweek, but there is a chance that he could recover in time for next weekend's Merseyside derby.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: November 25 (vs. Club Brugge).

Sunday's game against Man Utd came too soon for Ryan Gravenberch to return from a heel injury, but the midfielder might be able to make his comeback on Wednesday.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Hugo Ekitike is making continued progress in his rehabilitation from a serious Achilles injury, but the French striker is still expected to miss the rest of 2026.

It has been revealed that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Out for over a year with a serious knee injury, Giovanni Leoni returned to team training during the international break and is now in the "last part" of his recovery process, but a playing comeback before the Upcoming Year is still incredibly unlikely.

In a recent development, possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Likewise, Conor Bradley is finally back with his teammates on the training pitches after sustaining a severe knee problem in January, but it will be a few more weeks before he is considered for selection too.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

Drone operator apologises for filming Mauricio Pochettino's first training session, while Man United must apply to close airspace if they want to avoid another embarrassing security breach

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.

The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.

United suffered the embarrassing security breach on Pochettino’s first day as head coach after the 12-minute footage showing the Argentine and his staff working with the players at Carrington was posted online.

The owner of the account called CC Overview, who is known only as Colin, justified the intrusion by saying that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

United will have to apply to the Department of Transport if they want to close off the airspace to avoid more unwanted drones.

CC Overview took the video down on Friday morning insisting that he was unaware of the significance of his actions.

He also clarified that neither Liverpool – who are United’s opponents in Pochettino’s first game at Anfield on Sunday – nor any other club were involved in the filming.

Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session was filmed by a drone and the operator has now apologised.

The drone user, who is known only as Colin, noted he had not broken laws but apologised.

United have declined to comment over the incident and it’s unclear if the club have made contact with him or involved Greater Manchester Police.

His statement read: ‘I would like to speak about yesterday’s incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

‘My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

'I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

‘I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets.

In a recent development, 'I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match. I would also like to state that Liverpool Football club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday.

According to recent reports, ‘The video has been removed from my channel. I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well received responsible videos. Thank you.’.

United say they will not pursue legal action this time but will not hesitate to do so if it happens in the future.

To stop drones legally flying over Carrington, it has emerged that the club would need to seek permission from the Government to restrict the airspace around the training ground.

Footage of the session was captured close to Carrington and uploaded online.

Industry observers note that there are tight controls issued by the CAA and National Air Traffic Services over flying drones of different sizes, and a code of conduct related to how they are operated. It includes sharing photos and videos that could be ‘unfair’ to anyone.

It states that drones over 250g should not be flown closer than 50 metres to people, and drones below that weight should not be flown over crowds.

In a recent development, the drone and model aircraft code also states that you must ‘keep at least 150m away from residential, recreational, commercial and industrial areas’. It lists sports facilities as a recreational area.

There are also rules regarding privacy, which may well apply to United given that Pochettino and his players were preparing for a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday – arguably the biggest fixture in the English football calendar.

Industry observers note that it states: ‘Drones users must always respect your privacy and not cause a nuisance. They must comply with the same privacy regulations as anyone who uses a camera or recording device.

Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution.

‘If your drone or model aircraft is fitted with a camera or listening device, you must respect other people’s privacy whenever you use them. If you use these devices where people can expect privacy, such as inside their home or garden, you’re likely to be breaking data protection laws. Any photos or recordings you take may be covered by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

In a recent development, ‘Let people know before you start recording or taking pictures. In some cases, this will be easy. For example, if you’re taking a photo of family and friends at a family barbecue. In other cases, this will be less practical, so you must be careful to respect everyone’s right to privacy.

In a recent development, ‘Think before sharing photos and videos. Avoid sharing anything that could be unfair or harmful to anyone. Think carefully about who could see your photos and videos – especially before posting them on social media. Apply the same common-sense approach that you would with images or video recorded on a smartphone or digital camera.’.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was asked about the drone on Friday, saying: 'It shouldn't be legal. There is a reason why we train behind closed doors. It's not nice for any club.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a more encouraging performance against Dartford on Tuesday evening, Bridges knew that nothing less than three points would do if they were to stand any chance of remaining a Step 3 side next season. And it was the home side who started on the front foot, dominating much of the first half and creating a number of opportunities. Noel Leighton, Reece Hallard, Hayden Velvick and Charlie Bennett all went close inside the opening 25 minutes, but none could find a way past Cheshunt goalkeeper Rex Porter.

Against the run of play, however, the visitors took the lead. Hayden Neathey conceded a needless free-kick just outside the penalty area, and Joe Re stepped up to curl the ball past Sam Roberts. That familiar sinking feeling descended over Jubilee Field, and despite having enjoyed the better of the half, Bridges went into the interval a goal behind.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It has been revealed that but this time, there was no heads dropping. Bridges continued where they had left off, and their positive approach was eventually rewarded.

According to recent reports, after seeing an attempted lob saved by Porter, Leighton and his teammates finally found a way through, with the lively Hayden Velvick restoring parity. Picking up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area, the winger unleashed an effort which somehow found its way past Porter at his near post. However it went in, nobody in amber and black was complaining, and Bridges were back on level terms.

According to recent reports, the hosts continued to press for a winner, and debutant Jadyn Dundas should have put them ahead just minutes after coming off the bench. Arriving at the back post with the goal at his mercy, he was unable to get his feet sorted out in time to convert. What then followed was an end-to-end contest, with Sam Granville striking the crossbar for Cheshunt before Leighton and Velvick both saw efforts bravely blocked by visiting defenders.

This time, though, Bridges were not to be denied. Cheshunt failed to deal with the danger inside their own penalty area, and after Porter could only parry an initial deflected effort, the ball fell kindly into the path of Noel Leighton. The striker made no mistake from close range, sending Jubilee Field into celebration and, more importantly, putting Bridges 2-1 ahead.

Recent findings suggest that the home side looked relatively comfortable heading towards the final whistle, but injury time brought one final scare. An almighty scramble inside the Bridges six-yard box threatened to produce a late Cheshunt equaliser, with the visitors seemingly doing everything they could to force the ball over the line. Somehow, the Bridges defence stood firm and managed to clear their lines before the referee finally blew for full-time.

In a recent development, there was an enormous sigh of relief around Jubilee Field as Three Bridges secured just their third league victory of the season. A hugely key result for Jamie Crellin's side, and one which could prove to be a turning point in their season.

If the great escape is to become a reality, Jubilee Field must now become a fortress, starting next Saturday afternoon when Wingate & Finchley visit for another crucial encounter.

Bridges team: Roberts, Ferreira, J Hallard (Irving 75), Adeyinka, Neathey, Leighton (C), R Hallard (Dundas 65), Malone, Saunders, Velvick, Bennett (Idowu-Johnson 87).

Unused Subs: Villavicencio, Przybylo.

#140866. Industry News: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 47m • 📚 Deep Dive (9480 w)
